utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the outset let me give one decision. On the 23rd of March, the Prosecution filed a motion for admission of the written witness statements of Ronald Eimmers, and this was pursuant to Rule 92 ter. In its response filed on the 30th of March, the Defence defers to the Trial Chamber but requests to be allocated reasonable time for cross-examination. The Trial Chamber grants the Prosecution motion and admits the statement into evidence upon fulfilment of the conditions set out in 92 ter. The time originally estimated for this witness' testimony was two and a half hours. In its motion, the Prosecution estimates that the overall length of time required to be two hours. Accordingly, the Trial Chamber allocates 45 minutes to the Prosecution for examination-in-chief and one hour to the Defence for cross-examination. I'll just raise one other matter. On the 11th of April, the Prosecution filed a motion for leave to amend its Rule 65 ter exhibit list by adding 11 excerpts of video footage filmed by the BBC. The excerpts depict shelling and sniping incidents in Sarajevo were filmed by Martin Bell, witness W-157. Pursuant to Rule 126 bis, the Defence is entitled to file their response by Tuesday, 24th April. However, in the interests of expediting a decision on the motion, it would be helpful if the Defence could submit their response by Thursday, 19th April. Would the Defence be in a position to do this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The Defence has no objection. We shall provide our response by Thursday, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tapuskovic. Now, I understand the Prosecution had some matters to raise. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good morning to Your Honours. In fact, the first submission is exactly on that topic with respect to the videos excerpts. One of the excerpts that we have sought to add on the 11th of April to our exhibit list pertains to the first witness to testify this morning, and therefore I would ask leave to be able to -- to use this video excerpt with Witness 57. I have on Friday last week sent -- corresponded with the Defence for my intentions and also my intention to seek leave from the Trial Chamber, and I understand that my learned counsel has no objection to the use of this excerpt with this witness. But that is my submission with respect to this particular excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We will allow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next application is one pursuant to Rule 75 for protective measures. The Witness 116 who is due to testify this afternoon or after the first witness requests image distortion and pseudonym on the grounds that he is an electrical engineer and regularly travels in the Republika Srpska, and he is -- he is concerned that should be identified as a witness, his safety may be jeopardised. I have explained this to learned counsel, and I understand she has no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We will grant that application.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And if there is nothing else, we're ready to call the next witness, Witness 57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I'll just start by telling you that the Court has granted protection and, therefore, I will refer to you as Witness 57 and you should be careful not to identify anything that will identify to you the public. Firstly, I'm going to hand you a piece of paper with some personal details, and I would like you to confirm to the Court if those details are correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, this -- the particulars are correct. Yes, the particulars are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Once that has been seen, may I ask that be admitted under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 57 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will admit that the as P537, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 57, do you remember giving statements to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 21st of November, 1995 and the 16th of May, 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yesterday, were you given an opportunity to review and read over those statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And upon review of those statements, are you able now in court to confirm the accuracy and correctness of those statements, to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I read them in their entirety and whatever is contained therein is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I ask that 03 -- 65 ter 03106 be brought up on the screen and that it's not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 57, do you see a statement there and your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I was to ask you questions today, would the answers you give the Court reflect the contents of this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this statement be tendered under seal, and I note for the purposes of the record that in page 3 of the statement, the two substantive paragraphs refer to incidents that have been dropped pursuant to the Rule 73 bis order. So in line with your decision, those parts of the statement should not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes P538, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I now ask that 65 ter 03107 be brought up on the screen; again, not to be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 57, again, do you see a statement there and your signature on the first page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I was to ask you questions today, would the answers that you give to the Court reflect the contents of this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask if this could be admitted under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P539, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask a clarification from you, Witness. If we could go back to the first statement, that is 03106. And if we could move to the fourth page, taking the cover sheet as the first page, please. Witness, if you look on the right-hand side of your screen, you'll see the statement in your language, and I want you to concentrate on the fifth paragraph. Do you see the fifth paragraph there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Actually, in the B/C/S version, it's the fourth one. It's the one above that. But if you look at that paragraph above the fifth one, you see a sentence that says: "A witness saw the bomb being fired." Do you see that sentence there? And this is in relation to the 7th of April, 1995 incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Can you please indicate where it is so that I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: From my understanding of the B/C/S, I think it's the fourth paragraph and it starts --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what does it say, that sentence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: It was an old Bosnian house. A witness saw the bomb being fired. It flew for 15 seconds. There were more witnesses working in the field, and the projectile left smoke on its trajectory as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's fine. Now if we could move to the next statement, which is 303107, please, and if we could go to page 4. Now, Witness, if you lock at paragraph 16, that's on the top of the page, you should see a sentence that says, and I'm quoting from the English version: "They did not see the projectile being launched, just the activity." Do you see that sentence there in paragraph 16?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So in the first statement, you said that the witness saw the bomb being fired; and in the second statement, it is now said that you now say the projectile -- they did not see the projectile being launched. Can you explain that apparent discrepancy to the Court, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I can. After the event, there was talk that scouts, members of the BH army, had seen some activities in the area from which the projectile had been launched. Therefore, initially, when I made my first statement, I took it that they had seen it because I wasn't in charge, and I wasn't in a position to take statements from members of the army. I simply put it therefore in that manner, and I didn't specific that they simply didn't see it because I didn't have an opportunity to document this properly and accurately. In other words, I heard it from people, but I was unable to take statements from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you hear it from people that someone saw the bomb being launched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. The people who lived in Sokolovic Kolonija working in the field exactly saw the trail and the location from which it -- this modified air bomb was fired, and it left a very clear trail indicating the direction from which it came. Actually, it flew over them, and the people from Sokolovic saw from the north-westerly side a projectile coming, leaving a thick black smoke and emitting a strange sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you to mark these locations on a map in a moment, but let me ask you this, and, Mr. President, I don't believe this is disputed. You were a police officer for the Hrasnica police which was part of the Ilidza police station, is that right, during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court roughly how many civilians lived in Hrasnica during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Hrasnica, Butmir, and Sokolovic that were covered by the police station of Ilidza, or rather, the police administration of Ilidza had between 25 and 30.000 inhabitants before the war. However, during the war, a lot of refugees from Trnovo and Eastern Bosnia came, which increased the number of inhabitants up to 50.000. It was a very overcrowded area in a very small space.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And during your time with the police in Hrasnica in the war, are you able to indicate roughly how many civilians were killed because of shelling and sniping in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, I don't have exact numbers because we didn't keep records at the beginning of the war, because we were busy establishing authority organs. But between 800 -- sorry. 1800 and 2.000 residents were killed and between five and 10.000 inhabitants were wounded either once or more than once. So these are just rough figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And even though these are rough figures, what's the basis of your knowledge for these figures? How did you ascertain this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I believe that in a conversation with some people, they mentioned 1890 people, but they also told me that there were other cases of people who got killed. But these people were just in transit so the approximate figure varied between 800 and 2.000. I believe that the municipal organs have the exact figures. I didn't have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am sorry. Did you say 800 or 1800 that the figures varied between.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. 1800.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever -- did you or your colleagues ever review burial records from Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I think that these records were established only in late 1992. Prior to that, I believe that municipal authorities and the people from the Islamic religious organisations could have provided the exact figure about the casualties. I do believe that a municipality has these records, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. I'm now going to show you a map, and that map is 65 ter 02738. Witness, you should see a map coming up on the screen in a moment, and I'm going to ask you a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If perhaps the bottom left-hand side corner could be blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, do you see Hrasnica there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I can see Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: With the assistance of the court usher, can you take a marker pen and just put an H by -- or circle Hrasnica, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And then just put a H by the circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you also see -- are you able to locate on this map the Butmir-Dobrinja tunnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the tunnel in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you please mark the route the tunnel took in a dotted line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Can I have the map enlarged a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I think that if it's enlarged, the marking will -- can you see it on this size?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I put the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Excellent. Can you place the letter T, please, beside that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you also see the Igman road, the road leading up to Igman Mountain on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the road leading to Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And can I similarly mark it with a -- [French on English channel]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I think I'm receiving French translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, can you mark the road on the map, please, with a line, follow the route of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I would like you to, if you can, mark the confrontation lines; firstly to the south of Hrasnica and also up towards Ilidza. Are you able to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. With those two lines, can you with the letters VRS mark the area controlled by the army of Republika Srpska, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you know where the Famos factory is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you circle it, please, and put the letter F beside it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And which party to the conflict controlled the Famos factory? Was it the VRS or the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Three-quarters of the south-eastern part of the factory was taken by the army of Republika Srpska. Only a small part towards the Hrasnica settlement was covered by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you indicate on the map which small part was controlled by the ABiH? Is that possible? If you can somehow put the letters ABiH to signify that small circle, it would be most helpful.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you investigated an incident on the 7th of April, 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you go to the scene and conduct an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I went on the site; saw what had happened; went back to the police station; informed all the authorities, the judge; prepared a team to carry out an on-site investigation; and when I had a complete team, we went to the site and arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you see the site of the incident on this map; and if you can, can you just mark it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I can. But could Hrasnica be zoomed in on a little bit, please, so I can be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's actually not going to be possible because I would like for the purposes of recording the evidence everything to be marked on this map. But if you can just put a small -- a small S in the place roughly where the incident took place in Hrasnica, that will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I'll put a dot there and mark it with the letter S.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you did your investigation, and in fact from your earlier evidence about the -- about being told where the bomb was launched, where was that place from where the bomb was launched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: The place from which it was launched or the place where it landed?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: From where it was launched.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Let me mention again what I stated right at the beginning. I heard but was unable to confirm definitely that members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, who were on Mount Igman on the observation post, noticed that in the water works area, around Bacevo, something odd was happening, that there was a truck with some odd kind of launcher, that strange things were happening, and this is all approximate, but near the Bacevo water works building at Bacevo, which was under the control of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. And if you can see that on the map, can you please mark it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: It's not quite clear here. I can't see it very clearly, but I think I've marked it correctly. I have put a dot here. But if we could zoom in, I would like that very much, because it's hard to see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: From that dot that you have just marked on the map, can you draw a line to -- a line to the place where the bomb exploded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And on that line, can you place an arrow indicating the direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this map be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P540, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I now ask that Prosecution Exhibit 226 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 57, you see a document there on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see there at the top left-hand corner it says, "the SRK Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command, strictly confidential," and it is dated the 6th of April? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the next line says, "to the Ilidza Infantry Brigade." Do you see that as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And at the bottom, it is signed by Commander Major Dragomir Milosevic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want you to look at the bottom paragraph under the word "Order," and I want you to concentrate on the sentence that reads: "The most profitable target must be selected in the Hrasnica or Sokolovic Kolonija where the greatest casualties and material damage would be inflicted." Do you see that sentence there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: With respect to that sentence, if we're talking about Hrasnica, are there any military installations in the centre of Hrasnica -- or I should say were any military installations in the centre of Hrasnica in the period 1994/1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: In Hrasnica itself, there were no military facilities. There were some military facilities on the defence lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to ask you to stick to the centre of town, Hrasnica itself. Were there any military barracks in the centre of town in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: In the Hrasnica area, Sokolovic Kolonija, and Butmir, there were no military facilities in the settlements itself, either before or during the bar. We had no barracks in fact. The soldiers lived at home with their families.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you explain what you meant when you said there were some military facilities on the defence lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were buildings where those holding the defence lines changed shifts. There were such facilities. They held the lines and stood guard there, and this was along the demarcation lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How far was that from the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Referring to Hrasnica, it's the part towards the Famos factory, some 200 or 300 metres away from the buildings up to the demarcation line. The demarcation line was some 100 or 150 metres away from civilian buildings, houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry for interrupting, Prosecutor. I just would like some clarification, Witness. Could you tell me, whether, because I haven't really understood properly, whether the Famos factory was located in Hrasnica or in Sokolovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Famos factory was located in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said "Hrasnica," didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my last question to you: Is that where the battle took place, the battle which pitched the Light Infantry Brigade of Republika Srpska against the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so. There was fighting along the demarcation lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I now ask that 65 ter, or rather, Prosecution Exhibit 225 be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, could I ask you that last order from the SRK dated 6th of April -- I am sorry. I did not catch whether this has already been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: It has, Your Honour. It is Prosecution Exhibit 226. It was tendered through Witness Butt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, there is another document on the screen, and, again, it appears to emanate from the SRK, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command, and it's dated the 7th of April, 1995. Do you see that on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I apologise, but could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I just ask whether you see this document on your screen, which emanates from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, dated the 7th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could now move to the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, on this page, you'll see at point 2 the heading, "Our Forces." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the second -- the second paragraph or sentence reads: "In Ilidza Brigade, one 20-millimetre mine was fired and one 250-kilogram AB aerial bomb was launched at the centre of Hrasnica. According to the interception centre, the Muslims claimed that the Luna rocket landed." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, if I could ask that we go back to the map that was just admitted into evidence with the markings, please. Mr. President, I note the time, and I suspect that I'm over the half an hour allocated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I would ask, with your leave, if I could continue for a further five to six minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this is the map that you marked earlier on. And you see the circle around Hrasnica which you marked and also the dot with the S where you -- where you stated the bomb landed. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in the document we just saw, it said, if you recall, that a 250-kilogram aerial bomb was launched at the centre of Hrasnica. With your knowledge of Hrasnica, would the location where the -- the bomb landed, would that, to your knowledge, be the centre of Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And at that location, were there any military barracks or other installations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: The only thing that was located in the centre of Hrasnica was the police station, the police administration. That was close to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do I take it by that answer then that there were no military barracks or installations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, in that area, there were no military facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Now I want to bring up another document, and that is 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. Could you please ask the witness what is the approximate distance that -- from the launching point to the centre of explosion of this modified air bomb? How far did it actually go?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 57, I would like you to tell the Court the approximate distance from where the bottom was launched to the place where it exploded, if you can tell the Court that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Between three and a half and four kilometres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Anything further, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, that's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could now ask for 65 ter 02284 to be brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a document on your screen on the left-hand side, and it's from the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 1st Corps Command. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And it's addressed to the UNPROFOR Sector Sarajevo, Major General Gobillard. Do you see that there as well on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In the meat of the document, it says that the -- the aggressor violated the truce and fired, and I am paraphrasing, but fired 15 shells on the centre of Hrasnica from their positions and also used an aerial bomb with rocket motors, which was launched from a vehicle. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does this description of what appeared to happened in Hrasnica on the 7th of April accord with your memory and your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P541, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 57, in my last remaining five minutes, I'm going to show you some documents, and I just want you to comment on the -- the authenticity and the validity of these documents. The first one is 65 ter 787B. Witness, on the right-hand side, you will see a document in your language. Can you confirm to the Court that this is -- I ask that this is not broadcast, please. Is this your official report that you drafted on -- with respect to the incident on the 7th of April, 1995? And perhaps we could go to the second page and you can confirm your signature.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report that I drew up after the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I ask that this be admitted into evidence under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted. Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just one point of clarification, which page of the 65 ter document? It will be useful for everyone. Are we talking about -- I have it on a my list. It's ERN which ends in -- with 71, on my list. The 65 ter document contains several pages. Could we perhaps spell this out, and could we please be told which are documents which will -- which part of the document will actually be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva. What are the precise pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's precisely because of the need not to read out the pages in Court that we extracted the relevant pages; in other words, his report from the 65 ter exhibit, which was 787, which is a composite file, but I extracted the relevant pages for the witness, in other words, his report and other reports. So it is part of the composite Exhibit 787, but it's now been given the 65 ter number 787D, which just refers to these two pages for the moment, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So it would be just those two pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the moment these two pages, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sorry, B. B. Mr. President, what -- because these files, as we have experience before, are 30, 40 pages long and some of them include medical records, we had in the past just indicated to the Court officer the particular pages when we showed the witness. But what we have done in advance is we have actually extracted the particular pages and made them separate exhibits for the benefit of the court registrar. So that is why it is just these two pages, but they are taken from this composite Exhibit 787, which notice has been given to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit those two pages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, those two pages become P542.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, could you just please assist me with what was the date of the witness's report?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That would be the 7th of April, 1995, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And may I ask that this be admitted under seal, if it hasn't been done already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit it under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And for the benefit of my learned friend, it's pages 5 and 6 of the composite exhibit. The next exhibit -- 65 ter I would like to bring up is 787D, and I understand that these were pages 7 and 8 of the original, for the benefit of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, you see a document on the right-hand side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: This is a report on the landing of this projectile, and it contains certain elements of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, is this an official report from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Can you please scroll it up so that I can see the top of the page? Yes. It's a criminal investigation and forensic report compiled by the Ministry of the Interior, although this copy is not exactly legible and I can't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, you do confirm to the Court that this is an official report from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this document be admitted into evidence, and apologies to learned counsel, but the pages from the composite exhibit for her benefit are 46 and 47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes P543.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, lastly, Witness, I'm going to show you a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If 65 ter 03115 could be brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I see the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you recognise the place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is the place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: That's the centre of Hrasnica, and this is where the modified air bomb landed, the location where it landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you pinpoint exactly where the bomb landed from this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: This circle signifies what used to be a rather large, old Bosnian house, twice as large as this one, and the projectile exploded on the roof of the house. The house was completely destroyed, and I can see now that the owner has built a completely new house on that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And is there a school in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: This is the elementary school in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could you just put an S beside that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P544, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that is the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Isailovic to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. My name is Branislava Isailovic. I am a lawyer and member of the Paris Bar Association. I am representing General Dragomir Milosevic before this Court. I'm going to ask you a few questions about the statement which you have addressed with the Prosecution, and also I shall ask you some questions about what you have said today. I will ask to you pay attention to all of this, because please be careful to speak into the microphone properly and make sure that your microphone is not on when I speak. I'm sure it will be all right, and we shall manage it together.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have the same photograph up on the screen, the same photograph which the Prosecution has just shown us. This photograph was not on my list, but I believe it will prove very useful. I have no number for this photograph because it was not on the list which was provided to the Defence, so I would like a number from my learned colleague, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I respond to learned counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just provide the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Oh, the number, right. 03115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I would just add for the record that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You did provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What I provided was the DVD, which has a 360 degree panoramic video, and from there we take the stills. And, of course, the stills are taken once the witness has seen 360 degree video in proofing. That was on the list from last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let us proceed. We have the number. Can that be brought up, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to look at this photograph again. This is an aerial view. We can see a lot of new rooftops. Are these houses which were built after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: The big house that had been destroyed was built after the war, and all these houses were renovated after the war with humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that there was a lot of material damage caused by the war and particularly in Hrasnica. I presume that at the time this incident occurred on the 7th of April, there weren't very many houses in which you could live in at the time, is that right, in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: What do you mean there were many uninhabitable houses?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I shall explain this to you. You mentioned that there was a lot of material damage caused by the war. This incident occurred on the 7th of April, 1995; therefore, a long while after the beginning of the war, the beginning of the conflict, of the armed conflict. So this is my question to you: At this particular point in time, the damage caused by these military operations, did this render these houses uninhabitable?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. There were such houses, but most of these houses were unsafe to live in and, mostly, they were in the vicinity of confrontation lines; whereas, the other houses in Hrasnica, Butmir, and other settlements that were damaged as a result of war were the places where people did live, because they had no other place to live.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you were in Hrasnica all this time, weren't you, working as a policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you were an eye-witness to everything that happened in Hrasnica? What I have in mind are these military -- this military activity.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This military activity was quite intense in Hrasnica, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: That's correct; in all three areas, Butmir, Sokolovic, and Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that counsel specify when she talks about Hrasnica and other locations, whether she means the confrontation lines or the centre of town, because Hrasnica is a large area. I think the witness needs to be told exactly whereabouts combat was taking place -- where it is said that combat is taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it's for her to determine how she is conducting her cross-examination, and I'm sure she is aware of the size of Hrasnica; and if there is any point that you consider requires clarification, you may do so in re-examination. But please take that into account, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, a while ago you also mentioned the Igman Road; do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This road, Igman Road, how far was it from this house that we see on this photograph? What I mean is where this house which was destroyed on the 7th of April was located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: The house is approximately 200 metres at the elevation, or rather, 300 to 400 metres above the settlement is where the road runs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure if I what I heard is right, because I listen to you in B/C/S. I shall repeat my question. Perhaps you could listen carefully. We are going to talk about distance as the crow flies. What distance is there between this large house we see on the photograph where the former house was located, the one that was destroyed on the 7th of April? Just a minute, please, before answering my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see the word "as the crow flies" in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's there in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm sorry. I was looking at another line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, the witness is to answer the question. I'm not sure if he is aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please show me the first map of Hrasnica where I put my marks and where the road is also marked, and it will be much clearer for you then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is a good idea. I was going to show it to the witness afterwards, but we shall start off with this. Let's look at the map again, please. This is exhibit number P540, and this is the photograph which is a marked photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the map properly? Is it big enough?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, it's all right. Can I show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just asked -- put the question to the witness, and he answered by saying yes. I asked him if he could see it on the map properly. I would also like the witness to mark this map, and if my learned colleague has no objections, I would like to use a different coloured pen, a blue pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you draw a line which would be the -- the line from the place of impact and the Igman Road -- or, please could you tell us where the bus-stop was on this map and draw a line along that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Are you talking about the public transportation stop in Hrasnica? Which bus-stop are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I shall explain this to you. You properly remember that in your statement, you mentioned an incident that was then withdrawn and was no longer on the list of incidents quoted by the Prosecution. This was in October 1994. There was an incident that took place close to the bus-stop. There was a place where the buses stopped during the war. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to take this blue pen and indicate this on the map. This would be a section on the Igman Road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: It's a place called Osmice. The buses drove up to that point. And later on they would move into the woods to seek cover and avoid being fired at, and the forest provided this kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would like you to -- to put the letter SB next to the circle, please, and this stands for "bus-stop."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you please draw a straight line between the bus-stop and the place of impact indicated on this photograph, i.e., this house and the date of 7th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you please tell me what the distance is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: If we assume that between Sokolovic, which I will mark with 1, and the point of entry to Hrasnica is two kilometres, if I take this line, as the crow flies, then it would be around one kilometre to Igman. But this is already Mount Igman and where the forests begin.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you have drawn this line, according to what you remember. Could you tell me which road the soldiers of the ABiH used when they came out of the tunnel at [indiscernible] and took the Igman Road in the direction of this bus-stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: The exits from the tunnel usually took place during night, because in day-time there were no conditions for that; in other words, soldiers moved during night. They had to walk because was no fuel or vehicles for them. They walked in small shall groups through Butmir, Sokolovic, bridge, Hrasnica, and they exited at Igman and proceeded to their assembly point. So these were very small groups, between two and five people. There were no convoys because, as I said, we didn't have any vehicles or fuel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please mark this with a dotted line. Could you indicate approximately which road was used by these soldiers to reach Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: You mean from the exit to the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: This is the bridge, so some of them moved to Glavogodna. They took this road if there was no shooting. However, since there was random shooting during night, they would normally move and pass through this part of Hrasnica towards Tocilo, which is a ravine. But most movement took place during night because it was very dangerous to move during day-time. And the road between Glavogodna and Igman, this is the route that they took.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly, Witness, there were two alternative routes to reach Mount Igman, which we can see on this photograph, on this map, because we see two lines here, don't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: That is precisely so. There were two lines of movement. Whichever was safer, there was no shooting, then they would use that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I turn to the clock, and I'd like to put this question to you: I would like this photograph to be annotated and I would still like to use it. Do you think it's a good time to stop?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is it? Are you seeking to have it admitted? You would like to have it annotated?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I just stopped to ask this question about the break, because I would like to continue using this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You must also attend to the time that is left for your cross-examination. The Prosecutor used 52 minutes, and the Chamber will give you one hour. Originally, you were allocated 45 minutes and you have used 24 minutes so far. We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, we'll continue working on this map in front of us. In your statements, you also mentioned the general headquarters located in the area covered by your police station. Could you please mark on this map where these headquarters would be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It's not the headquarters, but it's the general area covered by your police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... Headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about -- no, the headquarters of the ABiH army that were located in this area, in the area covered by your police station.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: You mean the precise location of the headquarters? As far as I know, the command headquarters was a forward command post in the Igman area. The administrative part was in Sokolovic Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please mark the place where this building was located? I guess it must have been a building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: This was a row of houses adjoining each other; and as it is very close to the house I lived in, I will try to find it and mark it. I can only say that this was administrative part. As far as I knew, the command was in a forward command post at Igman because they were safer there, and they had better overview of the situation there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not very visible what you have just annotated. So could you please place a cross, and write an S next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: S for the B/C/S word "headquarters." Now, Witness, you -- during the war, you lived and worked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it could be clarified, but the witness has said on page 32, line 23, that the command headquarters was a forward command post in the Igman area. And I note that the S that he has just marked is in Sokolovic Kolonija which he refers to as the administrative part. So to -- to categorise that as the headquarters is possibly confusing, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, would you like to explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's like this: I'll tell you something very important. It's an important location on the map. It's called Golo Brdo, and it was held by the VRS. From that point had you a perfect view of all of the area under the BH army control; the free territory, Hrasnica, Butmir and Sokolovic. So that any movement, any grouping or military movement would immediately be observed and fired upon. For this reason, the command was at a forward command post in the Igman area as far as I know. People said it was at Kablar, which is where the main command was in charge of the operations, and that's where the commander was located. This place is Golo Brdo held by the VRS, and they had a perfect view. They could see any movement of pedestrians, civilians, vehicles, anything that moved.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have just talked about the excellent visibility from Golo Brdo, and I will ask another question because obviously you are well aware of the military situation at the time. Could you show me -- tell me something about Ilidza. Is Ilidza a plain or is it a slope?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: It's like this: The municipality of Ilidza, with the exception of part of Mount Igman which is up to 1.100 metres above sea level, everything else was flat. It was a plain. So that looking from Gavrica Brdo and Igman, you could see this whole flat area. You had a perfect view. You could see any movement any where in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to be more specific, you do agree that we're talking about part of Ilidza that was held by the army of Republika Srpska, and this area is a plain, is flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: No, no. Part of Igman, Golo Brdo, a dominant elevation above the Ilidza plain; also Gavrica Brdo, which was in the territory of the VRS above the sports airfield. The place is called Kotorac. You could see the whole area perfectly. You had a perfect view of the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that Republika Srpska held the plain where the Ilidza settlement was located as well as part of Mount Igman, notably Debelo Brdo and Gavrica Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Golo Brdo and Gavrica Brdo above Kotrica. It was all in Ilidza municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can we agree to say that from the part of Igman controlled by the ABiH army, the Ilidza plain was also controlled from that part where the ABiH army was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Correct, correct. Both sides had a good view of the Ilidza field, the flat area where there were areas under the control of both of the VRS and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the map. You marked a place from which allegedly this air bomb was launched. So this place, is it located in the flat part of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Correct. It's in the area of Bacina, in the flat part of Ilidza. You can see it on the map where I marked it. This was under the control of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you know anything about the 4th Brigade that was -- the 4th Brigade of the ABiH army that was located in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. This is the area where it was active, the free part of Ilidza. It held the lines in that area and fired from there. When I say "fired," what I'm referring to is the defence of this territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the person who commended this 4th Brigade at the time when this incident occurred on April 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. It was the commander of the 104th Brigade, Emir Redzovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you possibly remember where his HQ was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: All I can say is that in 1995 I saw him only very rarely, because in the area of Igman, Bijelasnica, and Trnovo municipality there was fighting going on; and to the best of my knowledge, they spent most of their time there. In 1995, I think I may have seen him only once or twice and then only in passing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I just get a clarification about the brigade because the question refers to the 4th Brigade and the answer of the witness refers to the 104th Brigade. Just if that could be clarified. In the transcript, at least, it reads the 4th and the 104th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are we talking about? The 4th or the 104th Brigade, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was called the 104th, but then it was renamed. It was the 104th Brigade belonging to the 1st Corps of the army of BH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to your recollection, Witness, this brigade included units that were subordinated to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. It consisted of battalions, three battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The -- I guess that these battalions were made of units, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could we see that all these people who made up the companies, battalions included in this brigade were made up of many soldiers. There were many soldiers that made up these units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: These were military-able local members of the population who made up these units.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like now to go back to the Famos factory. You marked it on this map, and I would like to know whether if you put Famos in the middle on the, one side of Famos you would have Hrasnica, and on the other side you would have villages, including Vojkovici where many Serbs would live. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, the village of Vojkovici with the hamlets of Grlica and others. The Famos factory ended where the village of Vojkovici began and then Hrasnica began after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please, just like you marked Hrasnica, could you please encircle in blue Grlica and Vojkovici and all these hamlets located next to the Famos factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please a V, letter V, next to the circle or in the middle of the circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you're familiar with this area. According to you, were there many civilians who lived in these Serbian villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Before the war, I often road my bicycle through the area. I would ride round the airport, Ilidza, to the source of the river Bosna, and the majority population was Serbian. There were little hamlets there inhabited mostly by Serbs. How many were there during the war, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But my question was not on the ethnic makeup of the village. I wanted to know whether the people living there were mainly civilians.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Civilians. But from what I learned after the war, the local population made up part of the armed forces of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Just like the residents of Hrasnica were part of the ABiH army. It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, with the Prosecutor, you talked at length about the this incident of April 7th, 1995; and in both of your statements, a lot of the passages are on this incident. Do you remember that on that day there were United Nations Military Observers in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that day well. The military observers had a house where they were, and this was in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the morning of this incident, do you remember having seen a number of these UNMOs at the place of impact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Before or after? Before the impact or after the impact?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: After the impact, many UNPROFOR vehicles arrived with military observers, and the observers who were in our area participated in the on-site investigation together with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember how much longer after the explosion you left the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: After the explosion, when we all fell from our seats, it was a very strong, dull detonation. It took us a few minutes to pull ourselves together and to have a briefing to decide who was to do what. I was the first to go on site to see what had happened. There was thick smoke and dust. In the ensuing chaos, we first tried to see whether there were any victims who needed assistance. When the dust subsided, there were two wounded people under the rubble who we managed to pull out, and I secured the site to make sure that nobody could enter it, no civilians; and then I informed all the proper authorities and also the military observers. I said as soon as a team is put together, the conditions are created, we will go and carry out an on-site investigation. From experience, we knew that after an incident of this kind, there would be additional shelling which often caused even greater casualties than the original impact. So we tried simply to conserve the site and put together a team, but we would not allow anyone to approach; UNPROFOR or anyone else. However, the site was conserved until the team could arrive there and carry out the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, after getting on the site of impact, do you remember finding the victim, Mrs. Ziba Custovic? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. We found Mrs. Custovic. Beside this house there was a smaller house, and the house had all about vanished. We found her dead, and there was enormous damage to her skull. She was taken to the morgue. .

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how the victim was dressed possibly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: She was a refugee, and she was wearing pantaloons of the kind worn by Muslim women; nothing unusual. We found her next to the cooker.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having found another victim on site, another victim that would be dressed in camouflage pants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I can't recall precisely, but let me tell you: Soldiers, when you were off duty, were at home, and they would put on whatever they had. The war went on for three or four years, and people were short of clothes. You wore whatever you had. He might have had them on, but he was at home. He wasn't on duty. He was sitting there with his mother. We found him under the rubble. Fortunately, they survived. We could hardly believe that they had survived. Their injuries were much milder than we excepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To be specific, you're talking about several people when you're explaining to us that this might have been a soldier that was just at home, or do you remember having seen with your own eyes a victim on site dressed in camouflage pants? So were you talking generally, or were you talking about what you saw that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: This young man and his mother, when we pulled them out under the rubble of the house, were taken to hospital. I can't remember whether he was wearing camouflage pants; but if you think he was, maybe. It's 12 years ago. At the time he was at home with his mother. It was in the morning. He was taken to hospital and given first aid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, you have another seven, eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this last topic is extremely important because in light of other evidence I believe that we now have an opportunity to get some information on other evidence that are in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are you seeking?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot control the answers given, and I can't really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You must know, as every lawyer does in the Tribunal, how much time you're going to take. How much more time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can only give you a rough estimate. I think I believe I need about 15 more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Isailovic, could you please ask the witness to tell us whether in this house the victim was found dead or not, and whether the young man was in the same house. I really don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I hope you have heard Judge Mindua's question, so could you please tell us, and tell us also if you're talking about the same house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: The victim -- no. Mrs. Custovic who died was in a small house next door, and that is where she was killed. In this big house that received the impact of the air bomb was where the mother and son were wounded. So they were in the house and they were found under the rubble. The woman living next door was the one who got killed. It was about five metres from the big house, towards north or north-west, so five metres from the house that received the main impact and she was found dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To be very specific, do you remember having -- having seen the person you found that was in the camouflage pant, did you find him under the debris, not moving?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has not confirmed that he found the person with camouflage pants on. In fact, if I recall his answer, he was equivocal in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is also our recollection, Ms. Isailovic. The witness did not confirm that, so reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. This was my last question because he wasn't very clear, so I would like him to confirm or to answer negatively.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that at the time you went to the location, following the explosion, you found people wearing uniform, camouflage uniforms coming out of the rubble, people who weren't moving?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, my submission is that the witness has already answered the question, and the answer was that he could not remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us hear it again. What's your answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is as follows: This young man and his mother, according to the statements that I took, were asleep in the house. This young man was pulled out, and I really cannot remember whether he had a camouflage uniform on. It was a huge commotion and destruction; and under such stress, I was unable to recall and record all the -- all the details. He was an asleep with his mother in the house when the projectile hit. Whether he had camouflage pants or whatever, I honestly cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But according to you, Witness, as you were a policeman in charge of the investigation, there was only one deadly victim who was wearing flouncy trousers, which are usually worn by Muslim women; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, Muslim women in pantaloons.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Just for the sake of efficiency. Do you remember having found on that location right after the explosion the commander of the 104th Brigade you mentioned a while ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I didn't see him on that occasion. I know that the commander had come just minutes before the on-site investigation but didn't attend. He received information about what had taken place. He came to the scene as soon as he heard about it, but I know that he did not attend the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the investigation was conducted on the day of the explosion, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But in the -- it was in the afternoon, around 3.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: As you remember the people who were present as -- since you mentioned them in your report, do you remember seeing UNMO observers there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you kindly repeat your question, please, Ms. Isailovic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they were there. It took sometime for a team, a KDZ team, to arrive from Sarajevo. They had to go through the tunnel, and the team included a judge as well. As soon as the team was complete, we visited the scene and sealed it off so no one was allowed access to it. Therefore, it took some time for the team to arrive from Sarajevo through the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you do confirm that in the course of this investigation, in the presence of the investigating judge and people from Sarajevo, the investigation started at about 3.00. A Norwegian officer and a British officer, who you mention your report, UNMO observers, were present at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: That is exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember what happened on the next day? Investigations were all conducted on the next day -- also conduct the on the next day. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: As far as I know, we completed the investigation on the same day, and I compiled my report on the same day as well. Whether anyone conducted any additional investigation, I don't know. But I do know that we finalised the investigation of the scene by 4.00. Whether anyone else did something additional, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And a while ago you looked at P542 with the Prosecution, but I'd just like to refresh your memory. This was a report prepared by the ballistics experts who analysed what was left of the bomb that had fallen. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Ballistics experts did their job.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember -- because after all you did sign this report. Do you remember what you took away for analysis was taken away on the day the investigation was conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, all the pieces were recovered from the scene, and they were taken for expert analysis. I received a report from ballistics experts, and I attached it to my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember whether on that day there were journalists present on the 7th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. There were reporters, and there was a big crowd, as far as I was, in the state I was, able to notice, and with all the work that I had to do. But I did notice that there were reporters. It was clearly seen that something major had happened in Hrasnica, and I did notice a few reporter vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you perhaps remember what these UNMO observers were doing in this location whom you mention in your report, which is dated the 7th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: You mean the ones who were with us during the investigation? Yes. They did take an active part in the investigation. Whatever we did, they did, too. And we endeavoured to recover the pieces together from the scene and to do the whole investigation together. We didn't do anything separately. They were all the time beside us, and we tried to be cooperative as much as we could and provide all the material evidence for their inspection that we found on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as eye-witnesses are concerned; namely, those people who saw the projectile in question, you remember the people working in the fields in Sokolovic Kolonija, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Yes. Many people had seen this projectile flying over. It was kind of miraculous. People talked extensively about it, but, yes, a lot of people saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you did not include what these eye-witnesses had to say in your report, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: Well, I said that some people had seen it. I should have gathered them all together and took their individual statements; however, in war conditions, it is a very difficult task to do. You don't want to expose people to danger. I think what we presented was quite sufficient and is not questionable as regards the origin of fire or the projectile coming from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself draw these conclusions; namely, on the direction of fire, where this air bomb was fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I mentioned the military scouts who saw precisely where this vehicle was and where something in the area of Bacevo was going on. Later when they descended, they explained what was happening there. As a civilian police inspector, I didn't have an authority to take statements from soldiers. It is up to the military security service and, therefore, I couldn't confirm or deny that because I couldn't take their statement. But I said that there were eye-witnesses, and many soldiers did see where the projectile came from because it flew over the field in this particular area. I'm talking about the modified air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, a long the same lines; namely, all these rumours that were circulating, did you get to understand whether the soldiers tried to neutralise the position from which this was fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-57
utterances.text: I learned later that a scout had sent a report to an unknown location at Igman where artillery weapons were, and that the commander of this artillery unit had asked permission to shoot warning shell, but the commander put a strict ban and prohibited any activity.
